ruleName: Relief Must Be Taken from Interference by No Play Zone
imagePrompt: Create a polished, modern, semi-realistic (about 75% realistic and 25% stylised) illustration in the established junior golf quiz style. Show a golf course scene with a fenced-off practice area adjacent to a fairway. A golfer stands just outside the fence, observing their ball which has come to rest inside the fenced area. The area should visually stand out as a No Play Zone due to physical barriers and course features, but do not include text, labels, numbers, arrows, captions, diagrams, badges, logos, watermarks, club crests, scorecards or speech bubbles.
imageAlt: A golfer stands outside a fenced-off practice area on a golf course, looking at a ball that has come to rest inside the fenced area, which is marked as a No Play Zone.

sceneSpec.setting: Modern golf course, with a practice area adjacent to a hole and clearly fenced off.
sceneSpec.players: One golfer standing just outside the practice area, observing their ball.
sceneSpec.ballPosition: The golf ball is visible resting on the grass inside the fenced-off practice area, which is marked as a No Play Zone.
sceneSpec.ruleMoment: The moment after the player discovers their ball in the No Play Zone, before taking any action.
sceneSpec.educationalFocus: Shows the typical scenario when a ball ends up in a designated No Play Zone, highlighting that relief is required.
mustShow: No Play Zone indicators (physical features only, no signs with wording)
Player looking at their ball from outside the fence

questions.title: Ball Stuck in a No Play Zone (Practice Area)
questions.question: Your ball lands in a fenced-off area on the course that has a sign saying 'No Play Zone.' What do you have to do?

choices.text: Hit the ball from where it is.
You can hit the ball or take a free drop, your choice.
You must take a free drop. Hitting from the No Play Zone is not allowed.
You must drop your ball and add one penalty stroke.

questions.explanation: A No Play Zone is a special spot on the course where you are not allowed to hit your ball. If your ball goes in there, you have to take a free drop outside that area. You can’t play your ball from a No Play Zone.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A place on the golf course, like behind a fence or a marked area, where you are not allowed to hit your ball.
You pick up your ball and drop it somewhere else (following the rules) without adding a penalty stroke.

questions.teachingTip: Show kids what a No Play Zone might look like on their own course. Use signs or ropes to help them learn where they can’t play from.
likelyMisconceptions: Thinking you can choose to play from a No Play Zone.
Thinking you get a penalty for taking a drop from a No Play Zone.

questions.title: Ball in a No Play Zone (Practice Area)
questions.question: Your tee shot comes to rest in a fenced-off practice area that the Committee has marked as a No Play Zone. What must you do?

choices.text: Play the ball as it lies.
You may choose to play it or take free relief.
You must take free relief. Playing the ball from the No Play Zone is not allowed.
You must take a one-stroke penalty drop.

questions.explanation: A No Play Zone is an area on the course where play is prohibited, often marked by the Committee and sometimes fenced off. If your ball is in a No Play Zone, you must take free relief without penalty under Rule 16.1f; playing the ball from the No Play Zone is not allowed.
